michelle: hey team, small onboarding oddity with juno7b->qwen-conv (int4). after running token-normalizer v3 we started seeing duplicate token ids for a few emoji/subtoken combos which leads to kv-cache collisions and weird repetition in long contexts. reproducible on 3/3 runs.

rajesh: hmm. which normalizer mode did you use (NFKC/NFKD/casefold)?

michelle: we accidentally flipped to NFKD in the conversion config (legacy fallback). command was:
```bash
python -m redwood.onboard --source juno7b_fp16 --target qwen-compat --quant int4 --normalizer NFKD --tokenmap auto-remap-v3.json --rotary-mode headwise-folded
```

olivia: oof. NFKD preserves some combining marks split from base char which can create different subtokenization. How does that create duplicate ids though?

michelle: two step sequence: 1) NFKD produced sequences like "e + ´" that downstream normalizer later recomposed differently, 2) auto-remap collapsed different unicode sequences to the same remapped id because remap was run pre-normalize in the pipeline. result: we had two different input byte sequences map to the same token id but with different byte-lengths, breaking rotary positional alignment for some heads.

marta: can you paste a tiny repro token trace?

michelle: pasted below (compact):
```
orig utf8 bytes: [0x65, 0xcc, 0x81]  # e + acute combining
post-tokenize ids (pre-remap): [10234]
after auto-remap-v3.json: [20345]
baseline (NFKC) tokenize ids: [20345]
BUT when remap ran earlier we also had an alternate path that mapped [0xF0,0x9F,0x98,0x80] (emoji) -> 20345 due to a heuristic bug. so emoji and e+acute both got 20345 after remap.
```

rajesh: so two distinct inputs became the same id -> kv entries reused -> rotary angles misapplied since sequence length expectations differ -> attention energy shifts -> repetition/hallucination. makes sense.

olivia: any metric diffs?

michelle: quick eval (longctx summarization 6k tokens):
BASELINE juno7b-fp16 (NFKC): rougeL=0.44, ppx=16.2
CONVERT qwen-compat-int4 (NFKD + remap pre-normalize): rougeL=0.29, ppx=30.5
repro behavior: early drift and repeating sentence fragments starting ~3.2k tokens.

marta: did you cross-check on gemma variants?

michelle: ran gemma-lite conv with same pipeline; gemma seems resilient — likely due to different headwise rotary implementation (gemma uses scale normalization at attention output). juno conversion lacked that post-attn normalize when folded rotary is used.

olivia: suspected fix checklist: 1) ensure normalization (NFKC) runs before any remap heuristics, 2) add tokenmap unit test that checks for id collisions on canonicalized unicode inputs, 3) add a small runtime assertion in serving that detects if the same token id appears for different byte sequences within a short prefix and emits a debug sample.

rajesh: also add a quick shim to remapper: when a remap would map two distinct unicode codepoint sequences to same target id, prefer emoji->unique id and shift the other one. basically avoid collision. but test-first.

ml-ci-bot: onboard-job-1749993333 queued: juno7b->qwen-compat int4 pipeline run (job_id=onb-4421)

michelle: created a tiny repro script and attached it to the ticket: repro-normalize.sh (runs tokenizer before/after normalizer and shows differing id maps).

marta: I'll take the kernel-side follow-up: add headwise post-attn normalization when folded rotary path is enabled. if that closes the gap we can push a hotfix.

olivia: please also add an onboarding step to the checklist: "normalize-before-remap" and a unit test that runs sample unicode sets +/- emoji. this should catch regressions on other model bring-ups.

rajesh: scheduling CI longctx run for juno/gemma/qwen after PRs: cc @ml-ci-bot

ml-ci-bot: scheduled: longctx-regression-suite for juno7b, gemma-lite, qwen-7b (run_id=lr-174999).

michelle: thanks all. will open PRs: one for pipeline ordering fix + tests, one for remap collision heuristic. putting the repro and metric outputs on the ticket. closing thread, will update with PR links. :v:
